walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociological Theories, Methods & Research — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociological Theories, Methods & Research brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociological Theories, Methods & Research.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Weber's concept for empathetic understanding of social action is:
options: Anomie
Verstehen
Praxis
Alienation

mcqs.q: Which research method involves in-depth participant observation?
options: Survey
Experiment
Ethnography
Content analysis
Religion is becoming more important globally.
Religion has completely disappeared from society.
Religion is declining in social significance in modern societies.
Religious leaders condemning immorality.
Ethnocentrism means concentrating on your own ethnic group only.

Judging other cultures by the standards of one's own — assuming one's own cultural practices and values are normal or superior. It is a methodological problem in social research as well as a social phenomenon.
Religious leaders condemning immorality.
Ethnocentrism is the same as racism.

mcqs.q: What is a moral panic according to Cohen?
options: Disproportionate media reaction creating exaggerated public concern about a group or behaviour.
Ethnocentrism means concentrating on your own ethnic group only.
Genuine widespread fear about a real, serious threat.
Religious leaders condemning immorality.
